about: Hand-editable seed data. size_gb = Q4 weights download; mem_gb = approx. memory footprint at ~8K context when a source gave one (otherwise estimated from size_gb in the page). lic_verified=false means the license is from general knowledge, not a fetched source. rel_ok=true means the release date was confirmed from a fetched source this session; otherwise it is from general knowledge and may be off by a few weeks. Single-source rows are noted: check the model card before relying on them.

models.name: Phi-4-mini Instruct
models.notes: Safe pick for 6 GB; GQA keeps the KV cache small at long context.

models.name: Gemma 4 E2B
models.notes: Ollama's default download is 4.6 GB (5.1B params with embeddings, 2.3B effective). One source lists a smaller ~2.8 GB Q4_K_M build. MMLU-Pro 60.0 per one source. Text, image and audio input. Verify license. Google says this Gemma 4 size can transcribe speech (clips up to 30 seconds), but Ollama's audio input support for it is not confirmed: an open Ollama issue reports audio being handled like an image.

models.name: Gemma 4 E4B
models.notes: Ollama's default download is 6.6 GB (8B params with embeddings, 4.5B effective), so it will not fit a 6 GB GPU on that tag. One source reports a ~5.3 GB total with a Q4_K_M build. MMLU-Pro 69.4 per one source. Verify license. Google says this Gemma 4 size can transcribe speech (clips up to 30 seconds), but Ollama's audio input support for it is not confirmed: an open Ollama issue reports audio being handled like an image.

models.name: Gemma 3 4B
models.notes: Best-supported small vision model in Ollama.

models.name: Qwen3 8B
models.notes: Strong instruction following. Keep context to 2K-4K on 6 GB.

models.name: Qwen 3.5 9B
models.notes: Multimodal. KV cache barely grows with context, so long chats are cheaper than on conventional 8B models. License not stated in sources.

models.name: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
models.notes: Largest conventional model that fits 6 GB, with discipline: ~1 GB KV cache at 4K.
models.rel_note: Ollama's page says Meta changed the license; confirm the current terms on the model card.

models.name: Mistral 7B Instruct v0.3
models.notes: More VRAM headroom than Llama 3.1 8B. Ollama's latest tag is Mistral 7B v0.3 (May 22, 2024).

models.name: Granite 4 3B
models.notes: Enterprise micro model; tool calling.

models.name: Granite 4.2 8B
models.notes: IBM Granite 4.2 (3B, 8B and 30B sizes). Thinking switch (reason step by step or answer directly), ~131K context, 12 languages, text only. Built for tool calling and JSON output.

models.name: Bonsai 2 9B (ternary)
models.notes: From PrismML, built on Qwen3.5 with ternary weights (-1, 0, +1). Maker lists a 2.0 GB footprint; Ollama lists 3.2 GB. Quality claims are the maker's and were not independently checked. Ternary models may need PrismML's own llama.cpp fork rather than stock Ollama, and an earlier larger Bonsai release drew complaints about speed claims: test before relying on it.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1 8B (distill)
models.rel_note: Ollama's 8b tag is DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B (the May 2025 update), not the January 2025 original.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1 14B (distill)
models.rel_note: Date is for the original DeepSeek-R1 family (this size is distilled from Qwen 2.5); not confirmed on Ollama's page.

models.name: Magistral 24B
models.notes: Source suggests capping context near 40K.

models.name: gpt-oss 20B
models.notes: MoE: only ~3.6B params active per token (from the model card, verify), so CPU offload is far less painful than for a dense 20B. Reported 60.7% on SWE-bench Verified (one source).

models.name: Mistral Small 3.2 24B
models.notes: Multimodal chat with tool calling.

models.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 7B
models.notes: The classic coding model for 8 GB-class GPUs; tight on 6 GB.

models.name: DeepSeek-Coder-V2 Lite 16B
models.notes: MoE: ~2.4B active params (from the model card, verify), so it is fast even when partly offloaded to CPU.

models.name: Codestral 22B
models.notes: Fill-in-the-middle. License restricts commercial use: check it.

models.name: Devstral 24B (original)
models.notes: The original Devstral (May 2025), fine-tuned from Mistral Small 3.1; 46.8% on SWE-bench Verified. Superseded by Devstral Small 2 below, which scores 68.0%.

models.name: Qwen3-VL 2B
models.notes: Lightweight general vision. 2 GB is the source's Q4 VRAM figure.

models.name: Qwen3-VL 8B
models.notes: OCR, charts, math from images. Too tight for 6 GB; fine from 8 GB up.

models.name: Phi-4-multimodal
models.notes: Fits 6 GB with little headroom.

models.name: SmolVLM2 2.2B
models.notes: Captioning, basic VQA, simple document reading. 256M and 500M variants also exist.

models.name: PaddleOCR-VL 0.9B
models.runtime_note: PaddlePaddle (not in Ollama); can run on CPU
models.notes: Document OCR, tables, formulas. Source gives ~1-2 GB.

models.name: all-MiniLM-L6-v2
models.notes: 384 dims. CPU-friendly, weakest accuracy.

models.name: nomic-embed-text v1.5
models.notes: 768 dims. Easiest general English RAG embedder on modest hardware.

models.name: granite-embedding 278M (multilingual)
models.notes: 768 dims, 12 languages.

models.name: mxbai-embed-large v1
models.notes: 1024 dims. Strong English retrieval.

models.name: bge-m3
models.notes: 1024 dims. Hybrid dense, sparse and multi-vector retrieval; multilingual.

models.name: snowflake-arctic-embed-l v2.0
models.notes: Multilingual long-context retrieval.

models.name: Qwen3-Embedding 0.6B
models.notes: 1024 dims (32 to 1024). Best quality per VRAM among the small models, per source.

models.name: EmbeddingGemma-2 740M
models.notes: Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 (Oct 2026): text, code, images, audio and video in one embedding space. About 567 MB with the full multimodal weights (191 MB text-only) per Google; Ollama lists 1.3 GB.

models.name: Qwen3-Embedding 4B
models.notes: 2560 dims.

models.name: Qwen3-Embedding 8B
models.notes: 4096 dims. Top open-weight retrieval if you have ~17 GB.

models.name: gpt-oss 120B
models.notes: MoE; Ollama lists a 65 GB download and says it fits a single 80 GB GPU. Active parameter count (~5.1B) is from the model card, not the Ollama page: verify. benchlm.ai's score for it fell from 40.74 (Nov 7) to 32.09 (Nov 10), moving it from 14th to 21st of its Ollama list; no reason was found, so check before relying on its ranking here.

models.name: Qwen3-Coder 30B
models.notes: MoE with 3.3B active params. Text only, supports tool calling. Ollama lists integrations with several coding agents.

models.name: Qwen 3.6 27B
models.notes: Reported 77.2% SWE-bench Verified and 83.9 LiveCodeBench (one source). Text and image input per Ollama (another source says vision does not work in Ollama: test it). Qwen says it beats its previous flagship (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B) on major coding benchmarks: a vendor claim.

models.name: Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B
models.notes: MoE with ~3B active params. SWE-bench Verified 73.4 per one launch write-up (vendor-reported). Text and image input per Ollama.
models.rel_note: Sources disagree on the exact day (Apr 2 vs Apr 15, 2026).

models.name: Gemma 4 26B-A4B
models.notes: MoE: 3.8B active of 25.2B. Text and image input.

models.name: Gemma 4 31B
models.notes: Highest vision benchmarks at this size tier per one source; strong LiveCodeBench/Codeforces per another. Text and image input.

models.name: Devstral Small 2
models.notes: Dec 2025. Built for agentic software engineering: explores codebases, edits several files. 68.0% on SWE-bench Verified per Mistral (the original Devstral: 46.8%). Text and image input. Needs Ollama 0.13.3 or newer.

models.name: Gemma 4 12B
models.notes: Text and image input. Wikipedia dates this size to Jun 3, 2026 but is inconsistent about whether it exists; Ollama lists it. Google says this Gemma 4 size can transcribe speech (clips up to 30 seconds), but Ollama's audio input support for it is not confirmed: an open Ollama issue reports audio being handled like an image.

models.name: Qwen 3.8 27B
models.notes: Successor to Qwen 3.6 27B. Text and image input, thinking and tool calling. Qwen's own model card (Qwen ran the tests; not independently re-run) reports SWE-bench Pro 61.7 vs 53.5 for Qwen 3.6 27B and Terminal Bench 2.1 73.0 vs 63.4; its GPQA Diamond score barely moved (89.2 vs 87.8). One reviewer saw 18-35 tok/s on a 24 GB GPU; needs Ollama 0.32.12 or newer. Only the 27B uses Apache 2.0: the larger Qwen 3.8 open models have other Qwen licenses.

models.name: Flint 40B
models.rel_note: Release date not found; Ollama's page was updated the day before this refresh.
models.notes: New coding-agent model: mixture of experts with about 2.5B active parameters, tool calling and thinking. Described only on Ollama's page; no benchmarks or independent reports found. Listed but not ranked until someone has tested it.

models.name: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B
models.rel_note: Release date not confirmed; Ollama's e4b tag was updated the day before this refresh.
models.notes: NVIDIA's compact vision-language model for local coding, reasoning and tool use (Ollama's description). Ollama lists the e4b tag at 7.2-7.9 GB. Larger 74B-A9B variant (25 GB) also exists. No benchmarks seen; listed but not ranked. License is OpenMDW, not Apache or MIT: read it before commercial use.

models.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B
models.notes: Tiny and fast: the size Continue's docs name first for as-you-type suggestions. Not meant for agent work. Size is approximate (a secondary source lists the base build at 986 MB).

models.name: Phonon (text to speech)
models.license: Apache-2.0 (phonon, English); CC BY-NC 4.0 (the 40M language models: noncommercial only)
models.runtime_note: Text to speech. macOS on Apple silicon only for now (Windows and Linux 'coming soon' per Ollama); needs Ollama 0.40.11 or newer.
models.notes: Text to speech, not speech to text: Ollama's speech blog (Oct 24, 2026) covers only text to speech. Tags: phonon (English, Apache-2.0) and phonon:40m-fr, -de, -es, -pt and -multilingual (CC BY-NC 4.0, noncommercial use only). Run: ollama run phonon "Hello from Ollama." (add --voice NAME to pick a voice; ollama show phonon lists them; > speech.wav saves a file). Apps can use the OpenAI-style /v1/audio/speech endpoint (24 kHz mono, WAV or PCM). Ollama says it is over 100x faster than real time on Apple silicon. The Ollama download size is not stated (0.1 GB here is an estimate).

models.name: Granite 4.1 Speech 2B (speech to text)
models.maker: IBM (Granite Speech team); Ollama upload by a community user
models.runtime_note: Community upload, not in Ollama's official library.
models.notes: Speech recognition and English translation. Transcribe a file with: ollama run gabegoodhart/granite4.1-speech:2b /path/to/audio.wav "transcribe the speech with proper punctuation and capitalization." Audio should be mono, 16 kHz. This is a personal upload on Ollama: read the model card and check who uploaded it before trusting it. I did not find Ollama documenting a speech-to-text feature of its own.

models.name: SmolLM3 3B
models.rel_note: The model card does not give a release date; the month is from general knowledge.
models.runtime_note: Runs in PocketPal AI on a phone; this page has no Ollama tag for it.
models.notes: Trained on 64K context and extends to 128K with YaRN. Extended thinking is on by default; add /no_think to the system prompt to turn it off. Size is the app's download size.

models.name: LFM2 2.6B
models.rel_note: The model card gives no release date (its technical report is dated 2025-11-28); the month is from general knowledge. Read the license for commercial limits.
models.runtime_note: Runs in PocketPal AI on a phone; this page has no Ollama tag for it.
models.notes: Its card says it suits agentic tasks, data extraction, RAG, creative writing and multi-turn chat, and advises against knowledge-heavy or programming tasks. Size is the app's download size.

models.name: Qwen3 1.7B
models.rel_note: The model card gives no release date (its technical report is dated 2025-05-14); the month is from general knowledge.
models.runtime_note: Runs in PocketPal AI on a phone; this page has no Ollama tag for it.
models.notes: Thinking is on by default; turn it off for faster chat. The card says not to use greedy decoding. Size is the app's download size.

models.name: LFM2.5 1.2B
models.license: LFM Open License v1.0 (assumed; the source does not state it)
models.runtime_note: Runs in PocketPal AI on a phone; this page has no Ollama tag for it.
models.notes: Described as built for fast on-device use. The smallest option here, so the quickest on a phone. Size is the app's download size.

models.name: Gemma 3 1B
models.rel_note: Date is the Gemma 3 family release.
models.runtime_note: Runs in PocketPal AI on a phone; this page has no Ollama tag for it.
models.notes: Text only (unlike the 4B and larger Gemma 3). The 32K context and license are from general knowledge, not a source read for this page. Size is the app's download size.

models.name: LFM3 1.7B
models.rel_note: Ollama's release notes added the LFM3 family on 2026-10-27; the maker's own date was not read. Read the license for commercial limits.
models.notes: Text-only, tool use and thinking, 256K context, from 1.1 GB to 1.7 GB depending on the build. Ollama's page calls it a model for local agents and fine-tuning and says it is not recommended for agentic coding or complex multi-step reasoning. Linux and Windows support arrived in Ollama 0.40.13 (2026-10-29).

models.name: LFM3-Audio 2B (speech)
models.rel_note: Ollama's release notes added it on 2026-10-27; the maker's own date was not read.
models.notes: Ollama's page lists speech to text, text to speech and speech translation in 18 languages, plus voice chat. Its release notes confirm text to speech now runs on Linux and Windows (0.40.13); the page only shows text prompts, not how to send audio in, so test speech to text before relying on it. Context is 32K in the spec table (125K in the tag list).

models.name: Bonsai 2 27B (ternary)
models.rel_note: No release date found in the maker's docs or Ollama's page.
models.notes: A ternary-weight version of Qwen3.8 27B at about a third of its 4-bit size. Ollama lists text and image input, thinking and tool calling. PrismML claims it keeps 98.2% of the full-precision Qwen3.8 27B's score on its own 14-benchmark suite (maker's claim, not independently checked); benchlm.ai's Nov 7 ranking puts it close to Qwen3.8 27B (53.56 vs 54.44 on Nov 10; 53.95 vs 54.26 on Oct 29), a third-party aggregate score. It uses new weight packings that need a recent runtime: Ollama v0.40.6 or later, and stock LM Studio may not load it. Also test the speed yourself: an earlier Bonsai release drew complaints about speed claims.

models.name: Ornith 1.5 9B
models.rel_note: Two articles give 2026-08-18 and 2026-08-19. Ollama's own library page names no maker or license; MIT is from those articles.
models.notes: Built on Qwen3.5 9B. Maker's own claims, not independently reproduced: 70.6 on SWE-bench Verified, 47.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 86.4 on GPQA Diamond. benchlm.ai's Nov 7 ranking scores it 33.6 (34.1 on Nov 5), still its top pick for the 8 GB tier. Download size is 6.6 GB.

models.name: MiMo V2.6 9B
models.rel_note: Ollama added it in 0.40.15 (2026-11-03); the maker's date was not read.
models.notes: Fine-tuned from Qwen3.5 9B on MiMo-generated data. Ollama lists text and image input, tools and thinking, and describes it as a model for code and agent workflows, including coding from screenshots. The page shows 6.6 to 8.7 GB depending on the build. No benchmark was read for it.

models.name: Qwen 3.8 Flash Next 125B (Unsloth 3-bit)
models.rel_note: No release date found; it was already on benchlm.ai's Oct 29 ranking. Unsloth's Dynamic v3.1 files are dated Nov 4.
models.notes: A 125B mixture-of-experts model that uses about 6B parameters per token (plus a 51B lookup table and a 4B prediction head, about 180B in all). This is Unsloth's 3-bit file (89.5 GB); their other files run from 66 GB (1-bit) to 111 GB (4-bit). Reading it from Ollama needs a recent Ollama that knows this architecture; Ollama's own library tag is a 105 GB Apple-only MLX build. Quantizing costs accuracy: Unsloth reports the 3-bit file matches the full model's top answer 88% of the time (its 1-bit file 80%, 4-bit 92%), which measures similarity to the full model, not task scores. The 15% accuracy gain Unsloth claims over other quantizers is its own claim and unverified. Qwen's own full-precision claims: 58.7 on DeepSWE 1.1, 62.5 on SWE-bench Pro. benchlm.ai scores the full model 55.69 (Nov 10; 56.12 on Nov 5). The license needs a separate commercial license for hosted AI services built on it. File size excludes the context cache, so plan for 10 to 20 GB more. Ollama 0.40.16 (Nov 9) says it now uses about 27 GiB less memory on Apple silicon (that is the Apple-only MLX build, not this file).
